source.title: Exploring Infant Gesture and Joint Attention as Related Constructs and as Predictors of Later Language

confidence_rationale: Longitudinal design with a well-specified 12-to-24-month prediction and standard instruments (ESCS, Mullen), but N=53 and purely observational, so a common social-motivation or caregiver-input confound is not excluded. Mapping fidelity held at 0.60: the outcome is a standardised language score, whereas ARC-101 asserts the emergence of a communication SYSTEM. Prediction is genuinely weaker evidence than bootstrapping, and the confidence reflects that rather than the study's internal quality.
failure_signatures: Unique predictive variance in an observational longitudinal design cannot exclude a common cause -- general social motivation, caregiver input quality, or maturation rate -- driving both the 12-month proto-communication measures and the 24-month language score.

The outcome measured is standardised vocabulary and language level, not the formation of a novel communication system, so a positive result is compatible with proto-communication being a correlated marker of readiness rather than the constructive engine.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In 53 infants, gesture use and joint attention measured at 12 months load on a partly shared underlying construct -- responding to joint attention being closest to gesture -- yet each uniquely predicts expressive and receptive language ability at 24 months on the Mullen Scales of Early Learning.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the developmental shape ARC-101 predicts: grounded pre-linguistic communicative acts (gesture) and shared attention are not merely antecedent to language, they carry independent predictive variance into it. If proto-language partially bootstraps from grounded proto-communication, human ontogeny should show exactly this -- the proto-communicative channel doing work that the shared-attention channel does not, and vice versa.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Prediction is not bootstrapping, and this is the central weakness of the entry. An observational design cannot exclude a common third cause -- social motivation, caregiver input, maturation rate -- producing both the 12-month measures and the 24-month outcome with no constructive role for the ecology at all. N is small (53), and the outcome is a standardised language score rather than the emergence of a system. Read this as consistency evidence, not as mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Typically-developing human infants; parent-infant free-play gesture coding plus Early Social-Communication Scales at 12 months; Mullen Scales of Early Learning expressive and receptive language at 24 months.

confidence_components.notes: Modest N and observational design cap source quality. Transfer risk is elevated because a human ontogenetic correlation is being read as evidence about an architectural bootstrap in an artificial agent population.
